title: RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
interviewAnswer: RAG retrieves relevant external context and supplies it to the model at generation time. A reliable RAG system depends on ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, context construction and evaluation—not only the LLM.
why: RAG is one of the most common AI-engineering interview topics because it combines information retrieval, LLMs, data pipelines and evaluation.
intuition: Instead of asking the model to remember all facts, retrieve relevant evidence at query time and put that evidence into the context. The model then answers using current, domain-specific material.
deepDive: A robust pipeline includes ingestion → parsing → chunking → embedding/indexing → query transformation → retrieval → optional reranking → context assembly → generation → citation/evaluation. Retrieval quality and generation quality must be diagnosed separately.
math: A common semantic score is cosine(q,d) = (q·d)/(||q|| ||d||). Retrieval is usually approximate nearest-neighbor search at scale.
code:
# Conceptual pipeline
chunks = chunk_documents(docs)
index.add(embed(chunks))
q = embed(user_query)
candidates = index.search(q, k=20)
context = rerank(user_query, candidates)[:5]
answer = llm(user_query, context)
commonMistakes: Calling any prompt with pasted text “RAG” without a retrieval system.
Evaluating only final answers and never measuring retrieval recall.
Ignoring access control and document freshness.
followUps: How do you choose chunk size?
What if retrieval returns conflicting documents?
production: Production RAG needs document versioning, ACL-aware retrieval, caching, observability, evaluation sets, latency/cost budgets and safe handling of untrusted retrieved text.
workedExample: For internal engineering manuals, index approved documents, retrieve relevant sections for each question, cite the source, and evaluate whether the correct evidence was retrieved before judging the final response.

lab.goal: Build a minimal semantic retriever, then show where generation would plug in.
lab.buildIt:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
chunks=['refund policy is 30 days','shipping takes 3 days','enterprise SSO uses SAML']
vec=TfidfVectorizer().fit(chunks); X=vec.transform(chunks)
q=vec.transform(['how long can I return an item?'])
idx=cosine_similarity(q,X).ravel().argsort()[::-1][:2]
context=[chunks[i] for i in idx]; print(context)
lab.useIt:
# Production replacement: embeddings/vector DB -> optional reranker -> LLM with cited context.
prompt='Answer only from context:\n'+'\n'.join(context)+'\nQuestion: return window?'
print(prompt)
